overall: The AG found the Selection Committee violated the Law by improperly using executive session to narrow applicants to one per position, failing to record the roll call vote in minutes, and inadequate executive session minutes; it found no violation on the roll call taking, location change, or detrimental-effect declaration, and no intent.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Selection Committee entered executive session without taking a roll call vote; the parties' accounts conflicted.
allegations.key_passage: Where the parties present contradictory accounts regarding whether the Selection Committee voted by roll call to enter executive session, and we find no clear independent evidence as to how the vote was conducted, we are unable to conclude that the Selection Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to vote by roll call to enter into executive session.

allegations.summary: The roll call vote to enter executive session was not recorded in the open session minutes, as the Open Meeting Law requires. The AG found this a violation, though the complaint did not raise it.
allegations.key_passage: Regardless of whether a roll call vote was indeed taken on the motion to enter executive session, it is clear that the Selection Committee’s meeting minutes failed to record the roll call vote as is required by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the subcommittee moved to a different room after the open-session procedural votes to enter executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Selection Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by holding its executive session in a different location than that which was included on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the subcommittee's executive session was improper because the chair lacked a reasonable basis to claim open discussion would harm recruiting qualified candidates.
allegations.key_passage: We credit the School Committee’s explanation and find that it has met this burden with respect to the declaration that reviewing applicants in open session would have had a detrimental effect in obtaining qualified applicants.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the subcommittee improperly used executive session to narrow applicants to one finalist per position, beyond the permitted preliminary screening purpose.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Selection Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by entering into executive session for an improper purpose when it reviewed applicants for appointment to the Search Committee and narrowed the field of applicants to one per position.

allegations.summary: The January 27 executive session minutes were found insufficiently detailed, merely listing steps taken rather than summarizing discussion. The AG raised this on its own; the complaint did not allege it.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the minutes are inadequate to meet the standard required by the Open Meeting Law because they do not offer a sufficiently detailed summary of the Selection Committee’s discussions

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the subcommittee intentionally violated the Law, citing its warning and another subcommittee's prior violation.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not find that the Selection Committee intentionally violated the Open Meeting Law when it improperly met in executive session to narrow the field of applicants to one per position.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Law's requirements by the School Committee.
Within 60 days, amend the January 27 executive session minutes, release them to the public, and notify the AG's office that it has done so.
The School Committee may not withhold or redact any portion of the January 27 executive session minutes.
